questions.stem: A patient was put on 20mg Hydrocortisone IV for an allergic condition. The physician decided to change it to oral methylprednisolone. The equivalent anti-inflammatory dose for 20mg of hydrocortisone in the case of methylprednisolone is:
questions.solutionHtml:
4 mg
  • 20mg of hydrocortisone, You need an equivalent anti-inflammatory dose for methylprednisolone.
  • From the below table if hydrocortisone activity is 1 and that of methylprednisolone is 5.
  • So hydrocortisone activity is 1/5th of methylprednisolone activity.
  • So get the equivalent dose you need to give 1/5th dose of hydrocortisone
  • 1/5th of 20mg is
  • So 4mg of methylprednisolone should be given.

questions.stem: The drug of choice for pregnant ladies suspected of having a baby with congenital adrenal hyperplasia is-
questions.solutionHtml:
Dexamethasone
  • The drug of choice for pregnant females suspected of having a baby with congenital adrenal hyperplasia is Dexamethasone as it easily crosses the placenta.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 314,315.

questions.stem: All of the following statements regarding corticosteroids are correct except:

options.label: A
options.text: Increase the concentration of neutrophils in circulation

questions.solutionHtml:
Inhibit the production of surfactant
Inhibiting the production of surfactants is an incorrect statement.
  • During late pregnancy, corticoids accelerate lung maturation and surfactant production in the fetal lung and prevent respiratory distress syndrome at birth. Two doses of 12 mg Betamethasone m.24 hr apart or four doses of 6 mg Dexamethasone i.m. 12 hr apart may be administered to the mother if premature delivery is contemplated.
  • Betamethasone or dexamethasone are preferred because of their higher placental transfer.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 310

questions.stem: The patient was on glucocorticoids for systemic lupus erythematosus for the last 5 years. Which of the following is not a side effect of steroids of long-term use of glucocorticoids?
questions.solutionHtml:
Loffler’s syndrome
  • Löffler syndrome is a form of eosinophilic pulmonary disease characterized by absent or mild respiratory symptoms fleeting migratory pulmonary opacities, and peripheral blood eosinophilia, and steroids are used in the management of it
  • It is not a side effect of steroids.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 317,318.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a contraindication for glucocorticoid therapy?
questions.solutionHtml:
Bronchial asthma

Corticosteroids are used in the treatment of bronchial asthma.

  • Early institution of inhaled glucocorticoid therapy is now recommended in most cases needing inhaled β2 agonists almost daily.
  • Systemic corticosteroids are used only for
  • Status asthmaticus
  • Acute asthma exacerbation
  • Severe chronic asthma is not controlled by inhaled steroids and bronchodilators.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 319

questions.stem: In the case of prolonged corticosteroid therapy for a pregnant lady, the preferred corticosteroid is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Prednisolone
  • Prednisolone appears safer than Dexa/ BetaMethasone because
  • Prednisolone is metabolized by the placenta and thereby reduces fetal exposure.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi,7th Edition Page Number:318.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old female was planned to start on corticosteroids for ulcerative colitis for 6 months. The patient was told not to stop the drug suddenly. Which of the following Measures will not minimize the risk of HPA axis suppression?

options.label: B
options.text: Use topical or local steroid preparations wherever possible

options.label: C
options.text: Give the dose divided three times daily so that peak steroid concentration is reduced

options.label: D
options.text: Switch to alternate-day therapy if possible

questions.answerText: Give the dose divided three times daily so that peak steroid concentration is reduced
questions.solutionHtml:
Give the dose divided three times daily so that peak steroid concentration is reduced

Will produce marked suppression of the HPA (Hypothalamo-Pituitary-Adrenal) axis.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 319

questions.stem: A 67-year-old with Cushing disease due to ACTH-producing pituitary tumors. He could not be operated on for a tumor due to comorbid conditions. He needs to be started on a drug which is a somatostatin analogue to control hypercortisolism. Which of the following is that drug?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pasireotide
  • Pasireotide is a somatostatin analogue, that inhibits ACTH secretion and reduces the circulating levels of cortisol in patients with ACTH-producing pituitary tumors.
  • Pasireotide is FDA-approved for use in those patients with Cushing disease who are not candidates for surgery or who have recurrent disease.


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st Edition, Page No. 2916,2963.

questions.stem: A 62-year male has been diagnosed with Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection by positive skin test and microscopic examination. The doctor prescribed him with corticosteroids. The patient can be having any of the following forms of except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ileocecal TB
  • Corticosteroids are contraindicated in Ileocecal TB due to the risk of perforation.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi 8th Edition Page No. 316

questions.stem: A 32-year-old male has been prescribed prednisolone in the neurology OPD. This drug is contraindicated in which of the following neurological conditions?
questions.solutionHtml:
Epilepsy
  • Corticosteroids are contraindicated in Epilepsy as it decreases the Seizure threshold and can aggravate epilepsy.


Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi 8th Edition Page No. 316, 319
